:::{#rem-measure-size}
#### Measures generalize size

A [measure](#def-measure) generalizes size:
it can measure how many elements a set has,
as in @def-counting-measure,
or how long a set of real numbers is,
as Lebesgue measure (@def-lebesgue-measure) does,
assigning each [interval](sets-functions.qmd#def-interval) $[a, b]$ its length $b - a$.
For example, the counting measure on $\set{0, 1, 2, \ldots}$ gives $\set{2, 3, 4, 5}$ the value $4$,
while the Lebesgue measure of the interval $[2, 5]$ is $5 - 2 = 3$.
Both can serve as the measures $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$ in the
[Fubini--Tonelli theorem](calculus.qmd#thm-fubini-tonelli).

:::
